scr_cash_bank_feed_configurations_list.purpose: Lists bank feed configurations — connections that bring bank transactions into RealPage daily — with status and linked accounts.
scr_cash_bank_feed_configurations_list.outcome: Treasury sees which accounts have working feeds and which do not.
scr_cash_bank_feed_configurations_list.rootCause: Daily feeds drive reconciliation automation and fraud detection; a broken or missing feed silently stops both.
scr_cash_bank_feed_configurations_list.ifSkipped: Accounts without working feeds fall back to manual processes unnoticed.
gaap: COSO 2013 — IT general controls over interfaces

scr_cash_adding_a_bank_feed_configuratio.purpose: Creates a bank feed connection and maps imported bank accounts to RealPage bank accounts.
scr_cash_adding_a_bank_feed_configuratio.outcome: Bank transactions for the mapped accounts flow in daily.
scr_cash_adding_a_bank_feed_configuratio.rootCause: Feeds must be mapped to the right RealPage accounts or transactions land in the wrong reconciliation.
scr_cash_adding_a_bank_feed_configuratio.ifSkipped: Accounts lack daily data or receive another account's transactions.
redFlags: Mappings not verified against account numbers

scr_cash_viewing_a_bank_feed_configurati.purpose: Views a bank feed configuration's connection status and the mapping between the bank's accounts and RealPage bank accounts.
scr_cash_viewing_a_bank_feed_configurati.outcome: Mappings can be verified when transactions appear in the wrong reconciliation.
scr_cash_viewing_a_bank_feed_configurati.rootCause: When a property's bank transactions show up in another property's rec, the feed mapping is almost always the cause; viewing it is the first diagnostic step.
scr_cash_viewing_a_bank_feed_configurati.ifSkipped: Mapping errors take longer to find and two recs stay broken.
redFlags: Accounts mapped to closed RealPage bank accounts

scr_cash_deleting_a_bank_feed_configurat.purpose: Deletes a bank feed configuration when a banking relationship ends or accounts are closed, so the feed stops importing transactions into RealPage.
scr_cash_deleting_a_bank_feed_configurat.rootCause: Feeds left in place for closed or transferred accounts can keep importing transactions, sometimes into RealPage accounts that have since been re-mapped, which pollutes reconciliations.
scr_cash_deleting_a_bank_feed_configurat.ifSkipped: Obsolete transactions continue to import and confuse active reconciliations.
redFlags: Deleting feeds still needed for open reconciliations

scr_cash_updating_bank_feed_connections.purpose: Edits a bank feed connection — refreshing credentials or updating account mappings after bank changes.
scr_cash_updating_bank_feed_connections.outcome: Feeds resume after credential expiry or account changes.
scr_cash_updating_bank_feed_connections.rootCause: Feed connections break when bank credentials expire or accounts change; they must be updated promptly.
scr_cash_updating_bank_feed_connections.ifSkipped: Feeds stay broken and daily monitoring stops.

scr_cash_viewing_bank_feeds.purpose: Views transactions imported through bank feeds within the reconciliation area, ready for matching.
scr_cash_viewing_bank_feeds.outcome: Preparers see current bank activity without downloading statements.
scr_cash_viewing_bank_feeds.rootCause: Continuous access to bank data lets preparers reconcile weekly rather than only at month-end, spreading the workload.
scr_cash_viewing_bank_feeds.ifSkipped: All reconciliation work is compressed into month-end.

scr_cash_notifying_users_when_bank_feeds.purpose: Sets up users (via their roles) to receive notifications when a bank feed fails.
scr_cash_notifying_users_when_bank_feeds.outcome: Feed failures are noticed and fixed quickly.
scr_cash_notifying_users_when_bank_feeds.rootCause: Feed failures are silent; without notifications, days of bank activity are missing before anyone notices.
scr_cash_notifying_users_when_bank_feeds.ifSkipped: Daily monitoring stops without anyone knowing.
redFlags: No users assigned to receive failure notifications

scr_cash_bank_feed_configuration_page.purpose: The page for creating or viewing a bank feed connection and its account mappings.
scr_cash_bank_feed_configuration_page.rootCause: Accurate mapping on this page determines which reconciliation each bank transaction lands in.
scr_cash_bank_feed_configuration_page.ifSkipped: Feeds are mis-mapped and transactions land in the wrong property's reconciliation.
redFlags: Unmapped bank accounts in the feed

scr_cash_positive_pay_configuration_list.purpose: Lists positive pay configurations — the file layouts and transmission settings each bank requires — for accounts that issue checks.
scr_cash_positive_pay_configuration_list.outcome: Every check-issuing account has a positive pay setup.
scr_cash_positive_pay_configuration_list.rootCause: Positive pay only works if configured for each issuing account in the bank's required format; gaps leave accounts exposed to check fraud.
scr_cash_positive_pay_configuration_list.ifSkipped: Some accounts issue checks without positive pay protection.
gaap: UCC 3-406 / 4-406 — loss allocation for check fraud
redFlags: Check-issuing accounts missing from the list

scr_cash_positive_pay_overview.purpose: Explains positive pay: an automated fraud prevention service where the company sends the bank a list of issued checks and the bank only pays checks that match number, amount (and often payee).
scr_cash_positive_pay_overview.outcome: Users understand why every check run must be reported to the bank.
scr_cash_positive_pay_overview.rootCause: Check fraud (altered, counterfeit, washed checks) is widespread; banks increasingly shift losses to customers who do not use positive pay.
scr_cash_positive_pay_overview.ifSkipped: Accounts remain exposed to check fraud with little recourse against the bank.
redFlags: Payee positive pay not enabled where the bank offers it

scr_cash_adding_a_positive_pay_configura.purpose: Creates a positive pay configuration for a bank account — file layout, transmission method and schedule.
scr_cash_adding_a_positive_pay_configura.outcome: Positive pay files are generated for the account automatically.
scr_cash_adding_a_positive_pay_configura.rootCause: Each bank specifies its own positive pay format; configuration makes files acceptable to the bank.
scr_cash_adding_a_positive_pay_configura.ifSkipped: Files cannot be generated for the account.
redFlags: Configurations not tested with the bank

scr_cash_overriding_bank_layout_specific.purpose: Overrides the standard CSV layout for positive pay files to match a bank's specific requirements (column order, date format, void indicators).
scr_cash_overriding_bank_layout_specific.outcome: Positive pay files are accepted by banks with non-standard formats.
scr_cash_overriding_bank_layout_specific.rootCause: Banks, especially regional ones, use custom CSV specs; without overrides files are rejected and checks are unprotected.
scr_cash_overriding_bank_layout_specific.ifSkipped: Positive pay files are rejected and checks go unprotected.
redFlags: Void indicators missing, so voided checks remain payable

scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_positive_p.purpose: Reviews or updates a positive pay configuration — file layout, included accounts, transmission method and schedule — when the bank changes its format or cut-off.
scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_positive_p.outcome: Positive pay continues working after bank changes.
scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_positive_p.rootCause: Banks periodically change positive pay file formats, upload channels and daily cut-off times. If the configuration is not updated to match, files are rejected or arrive late and the day's checks are unprotected.
scr_cash_viewing_or_editing_a_positive_p.ifSkipped: Files fail silently and checks lose protection.
redFlags: Edits without confirming acceptance by the bank

scr_cash_deleting_and_inactivating_posit.purpose: Deletes or inactivates positive pay configurations for accounts that no longer issue checks.
scr_cash_deleting_and_inactivating_posit.outcome: Positive pay setup reflects current check-issuing accounts.
scr_cash_deleting_and_inactivating_posit.rootCause: Inactivating configurations for closed accounts avoids failed transmissions; inactivating one for an active account would remove fraud protection.
scr_cash_deleting_and_inactivating_posit.ifSkipped: Failed transmissions for closed accounts; misuse removes protection.
redFlags: Inactivated configurations on accounts still issuing checks

scr_cash_positive_pay_configuration_page.purpose: The page defining a positive pay configuration — bank, accounts, layout, transmission and schedule.
scr_cash_positive_pay_configuration_page.outcome: A complete positive pay setup for the selected accounts.
scr_cash_positive_pay_configuration_page.rootCause: Every element (accounts included, schedule) determines whether checks are protected when issued.
scr_cash_positive_pay_configuration_page.ifSkipped: Accounts or schedules are incomplete and some checks go out unprotected.
redFlags: Schedules running after the bank's positive pay cut-off

scr_cash_check_update_page.purpose: Page to change the signatures and templates printed on checks for bank accounts.
scr_cash_check_update_page.outcome: Checks carry current authorized signatures and correct templates.
scr_cash_check_update_page.rootCause: When authorized signers change (a controller leaves), checks must stop printing the old signature immediately; signature images are sensitive controls.
scr_cash_check_update_page.ifSkipped: Checks print with signatures of people no longer authorized.
redFlags: Signature updates without matching bank signature card changes

scr_cash_updating_a_check_signature.purpose: Uploads or replaces the signature image printed on checks for a bank account — for example when a controller or authorized signer leaves and the bank signature card changes.
scr_cash_updating_a_check_signature.outcome: Checks carry the current authorized signer's signature.
scr_cash_updating_a_check_signature.rootCause: Signature images must match the bank's signature card; changes are security-sensitive because anyone with access can print signed checks.
scr_cash_updating_a_check_signature.ifSkipped: Checks are signed by unauthorized or former signers.
gaap: COSO 2013 — access controls over signature images
redFlags: Signature changes by users without treasury authority

scr_cash_updating_a_check_template.purpose: Changes the check template (layout, MICR placement, logo) used for printing checks from a bank account.
scr_cash_updating_a_check_template.outcome: Checks print in a format the bank accepts.
scr_cash_updating_a_check_template.rootCause: Incorrect MICR placement causes bank processing failures; templates must match check stock and bank specs.
scr_cash_updating_a_check_template.ifSkipped: Checks are rejected or processed incorrectly.
redFlags: Template changes not tested on sample checks

scr_cash_design_custom_check_layouts_lis.purpose: Lists the custom check layouts designed for the company's own check stock (for example security stock with watermark and branded header), for viewing, editing or deleting.
scr_cash_design_custom_check_layouts_lis.outcome: Available layouts for printing checks on custom stock.
scr_cash_design_custom_check_layouts_lis.rootCause: Companies with branded or security-feature check stock need custom layouts that align fields with the stock.
scr_cash_design_custom_check_layouts_lis.ifSkipped: Checks print misaligned on custom stock.

scr_cash_designing_a_custom_check_layout.purpose: Designs a custom check layout — uploading the company's layout and positioning fields such as payee, amount, date and MICR line.
scr_cash_designing_a_custom_check_layout.outcome: Checks print correctly on the company's check stock.
scr_cash_designing_a_custom_check_layout.rootCause: Custom stock with security features requires precise field placement for bank processing and fraud resistance.
scr_cash_designing_a_custom_check_layout.ifSkipped: Checks are unreadable by bank scanners or misaligned.
redFlags: MICR line position not validated with the bank

scr_cash_custom_check_components.purpose: Describes the components of a custom check (payee, amount in words and figures, date, memo, signature, MICR) and how they appear.
scr_cash_custom_check_components.rootCause: Missing or misplaced components (like amount in words) make checks non-negotiable or easier to alter.
scr_cash_custom_check_components.ifSkipped: Checks missing required components are rejected.
redFlags: Layouts missing the amount in words

scr_cash_fixing_check_alignment.purpose: Adjusts check layout offsets so printed text aligns with the fields on the check stock.
scr_cash_fixing_check_alignment.outcome: Checks print cleanly within the pre-printed fields.
scr_cash_fixing_check_alignment.rootCause: Printer differences shift output; misaligned checks are rejected by vendors' banks or look altered.
scr_cash_fixing_check_alignment.ifSkipped: Checks are reprinted, wasting stock and creating void sequence gaps.

scr_cash_updating_the_company_name_or_ad.purpose: Updates the payer name or address printed on checks for a bank account, typically after an entity name change or relocation.
scr_cash_updating_the_company_name_or_ad.outcome: Checks show the correct legal entity and address.
scr_cash_updating_the_company_name_or_ad.rootCause: Checks must show the legal entity that owns the account; mismatches confuse vendors and banks and can cause returns.
scr_cash_updating_the_company_name_or_ad.ifSkipped: Checks show outdated entity names, causing confusion and potential rejections.
redFlags: Entity name on checks different from bank account title

scr_cash_viewing_a_custom_check_layout.purpose: Opens an existing custom check layout to check the position of payee, amount, date, signature and MICR fields before a check run is printed.
scr_cash_viewing_a_custom_check_layout.outcome: Layouts can be reviewed before use or during troubleshooting of misprints.
scr_cash_viewing_a_custom_check_layout.rootCause: Reviewing a layout before a large check run avoids printing, voiding and reprinting hundreds of checks — and the gaps in check sequence that follow, which auditors then question.
scr_cash_viewing_a_custom_check_layout.ifSkipped: Layout problems are found only after printing a run.

scr_cash_editing_a_custom_check_layout.purpose: Edits the fields or positions of a custom check layout — for example after the company orders new check stock from a different printer.
scr_cash_editing_a_custom_check_layout.outcome: Layouts corrected for stock or bank changes before the next check run.
scr_cash_editing_a_custom_check_layout.rootCause: New check stock or new bank MICR requirements shift where fields must print. Editing the layout, and test-printing it, prevents a whole check run from being misprinted.
scr_cash_editing_a_custom_check_layout.ifSkipped: Checks print incorrectly on the new stock and must be voided and reprinted.

scr_cash_deleting_a_custom_check_layout.purpose: Deletes a custom check layout that is no longer used, such as one designed for check stock the company has retired.
scr_cash_deleting_a_custom_check_layout.outcome: Only current layouts can be selected for printing.
scr_cash_deleting_a_custom_check_layout.rootCause: Obsolete layouts remain selectable and can be picked by mistake during a check run, printing fields in the wrong places on the current stock.
scr_cash_deleting_a_custom_check_layout.ifSkipped: A retired layout is used for a check run and the checks must be voided and reprinted.
redFlags: Deleting layouts assigned to active accounts

scr_cash_design_custom_check_layout_page.purpose: The designer page for creating or viewing a custom check layout, where each check component is positioned precisely on the company's check stock.
scr_cash_design_custom_check_layout_page.outcome: A precise layout definition for printing.
scr_cash_design_custom_check_layout_page.rootCause: A dedicated designer allows exact positioning for security stock and MICR compliance.
scr_cash_design_custom_check_layout_page.ifSkipped: Layouts are approximated and checks misprint.

scr_cash_owner_distribution_list.purpose: Lists owner distribution records — the details of distributions of property cash to owners or partners (amount, date, owner, bank account).
scr_cash_owner_distribution_list.outcome: A record of cash returned to owners that ties to equity and cash.
scr_cash_owner_distribution_list.rootCause: Distributions reduce partners' capital and must follow the operating agreement's waterfall; a record is needed for capital account reporting and K-1s.
scr_cash_owner_distribution_list.ifSkipped: Distributions are recorded inconsistently and capital accounts cannot be reconciled.

scr_cash_adding_an_owner_distribution.purpose: Records an owner distribution — owner, amount, date and source bank account — posting DR Distributions / CR Cash.
scr_cash_adding_an_owner_distribution.outcome: The distribution is reflected in cash and equity.
scr_cash_adding_an_owner_distribution.rootCause: Distributions must be recorded as equity reductions, not expenses, and tied to approved available cash calculations.
scr_cash_adding_an_owner_distribution.ifSkipped: Distributions are misrecorded as expenses or not recorded.

scr_cash_viewing_an_owner_distribution.purpose: Views the details of a recorded owner distribution — owner or partner, amount, date and source bank account — to answer partner inquiries or reconcile capital accounts.
scr_cash_viewing_an_owner_distribution.outcome: Distribution details are available for owner inquiries and capital account reconciliations.
scr_cash_viewing_an_owner_distribution.rootCause: Partners and fund accountants reconcile capital accounts quarterly and at year-end for K-1s; they need distribution detail that ties to the cash that left the property.
scr_cash_viewing_an_owner_distribution.ifSkipped: Distribution inquiries take longer and capital account differences go unresolved.

scr_cash_deleting_an_owner_distribution.purpose: Deletes an owner distribution record that was entered in error (duplicate or wrong owner) before it affects equity reporting.
scr_cash_deleting_an_owner_distribution.rootCause: Duplicate distribution records overstate distributions and misstate partners' capital accounts, which flow to K-1s and investor statements.
scr_cash_deleting_an_owner_distribution.ifSkipped: Capital accounts are misstated for distributions that never happened.
redFlags: Deleting distributions that were actually paid

scr_cash_owner_distribution_page.purpose: The page used to record an owner distribution's details — owner, amount, distribution date, source bank account and memo.
scr_cash_owner_distribution_page.outcome: A complete distribution record that supports capital account statements.
scr_cash_owner_distribution_page.rootCause: Complete records (owner, date, amount, bank) are needed for capital account statements, waterfall calculations and K-1 preparation.
scr_cash_owner_distribution_page.ifSkipped: Incomplete distribution records make capital accounts and K-1s hard to support.

scr_cash_holdback_categories.purpose: Manages categories of holdbacks — security deposits, operating reserves, lender minimums, accrued payables — used in available cash.
scr_cash_holdback_categories.rootCause: Standard categories make available cash comparable across properties and understandable to owners.
scr_cash_holdback_categories.ifSkipped: Holdbacks are labeled inconsistently and owners cannot compare properties.

scr_cash_adding_a_holdback_category.purpose: Adds a new holdback category — for example 'Insurance Deductible Reserve' after an owner raises its deductible, or 'Tax Appeal Reserve' during a property tax appeal.
scr_cash_adding_a_holdback_category.outcome: New types of cash restrictions can be tracked.
scr_cash_adding_a_holdback_category.rootCause: Owners and lenders introduce new cash restrictions over time — a higher insurance deductible, a tax appeal, a lender-required operating reserve. Each needs its own category so available cash withholds it explicitly.
scr_cash_adding_a_holdback_category.ifSkipped: New restrictions are not reflected in available cash.

scr_cash_editing_a_holdback_category.purpose: Edits a holdback category's name or settings, for example renaming a generic reserve category to match the owner's terminology.
scr_cash_editing_a_holdback_category.outcome: Holdback categories stay aligned with current policies.
scr_cash_editing_a_holdback_category.rootCause: Policies evolve; category settings must follow so available cash remains accurate.

scr_cash_deleting_a_holdback_category.purpose: Deletes a holdback category that is no longer used, such as a reserve requirement from a loan that has been repaid.
scr_cash_deleting_a_holdback_category.outcome: Obsolete categories removed from available cash.
scr_cash_deleting_a_holdback_category.rootCause: Unused categories clutter reports; deleting one in use would remove a restriction from available cash.

scr_cash_holdbacks.purpose: Manages holdbacks — amounts of cash designated to pay anticipated obligations (upcoming tax installment, insurance renewal, capital project) — that reduce available cash.
scr_cash_holdbacks.outcome: Known upcoming obligations are protected from distribution.
scr_cash_holdbacks.rootCause: Large known payments (semi-annual taxes, insurance renewals) must be reserved in advance; otherwise cash is distributed and a capital call follows.
scr_cash_holdbacks.ifSkipped: Cash is distributed and the property cannot pay its tax or insurance bill.
redFlags: No holdback ahead of a known tax installment

scr_cash_adding_a_holdback.purpose: Adds a holdback — an anticipated obligation amount — for a location, reducing its available cash.
scr_cash_adding_a_holdback.rootCause: Anticipated obligations are not yet in A/P; holdbacks capture them for distribution decisions.

scr_cash_viewing_and_editing_holdbacks.purpose: Views or updates holdbacks for a location as obligations change or are paid — for example releasing the tax installment holdback once the tax bill is paid.
scr_cash_viewing_and_editing_holdbacks.rootCause: Once an obligation is paid, its holdback must be released or cash is withheld unnecessarily.
scr_cash_viewing_and_editing_holdbacks.ifSkipped: Paid obligations keep reducing available cash.

scr_cash_about_cash_management.purpose: Quick Steps overview of Cash Management for managing corporate cash accounts, deposits, transfers, payments and reconciliations.
scr_cash_about_cash_management.outcome: New users get a condensed map of cash tasks.
scr_cash_about_cash_management.rootCause: Offshore staff rotate often; a short overview gets them productive on cash tasks quickly.
scr_cash_about_cash_management.ifSkipped: New staff misuse screens and create rec breaks.
redFlags: New staff posting cash via JEs

scr_cash_adding_a_bank_account_2.purpose: Quick Steps for adding a bank account: enter bank details, map the GL cash account and posting journals, set entity restrictions and check/electronic payment settings.
scr_cash_adding_a_bank_account_2.outcome: A new account set up quickly with correct GL mapping and restrictions.
scr_cash_adding_a_bank_account_2.rootCause: Acquisitions and refinancings require new accounts on short notice. The quick path focuses on the settings that cause the most damage when wrong — GL mapping and entity restriction.
scr_cash_adding_a_bank_account_2.ifSkipped: Accounts are set up with wrong mappings, misposting every future transaction.
redFlags: Trust accounts mapped to operating cash

scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_account_2.purpose: Quick Steps for creating a credit card account — card ID, last four digits, issuer and liability GL — so card charges can be entered and reconciled.
scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_account_2.outcome: Card accounts ready for recording and reconciling charges.
scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_account_2.rootCause: A card account must exist in RealPage before any charges can be recorded, coded to properties and reconciled to the issuer statement; cards issued before setup create a backlog of unrecorded spend.
scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_account_2.ifSkipped: Card charges pile up unrecorded until the account is created, then land in the wrong month.

scr_cash_adding_a_deposit_2.purpose: Quick Steps for creating a deposit from payments sitting in undeposited funds, so the deposit in RealPage matches the deposit slip and the bank's credit.
scr_cash_adding_a_deposit_2.outcome: Receipts moved to the bank account in a deposit that matches the bank.
scr_cash_adding_a_deposit_2.rootCause: Daily deposits are routine for site staff; a short, consistent procedure keeps deposits matching bank credits and keeps undeposited funds near zero.
scr_cash_adding_a_deposit_2.ifSkipped: Undeposited funds accumulate and deposits no longer match bank credits.

scr_cash_transferring_funds.purpose: Quick Steps for moving funds between the company's bank accounts, including cash sweeps to concentration accounts and funding for owner distributions.
scr_cash_transferring_funds.outcome: Transfers recorded on both sides consistently.
scr_cash_transferring_funds.rootCause: Transfers are frequent; the quick path ensures both legs are recorded in one transaction.
scr_cash_transferring_funds.ifSkipped: One-sided transfers break two bank reconciliations at once.

scr_cash_reversing_a_deposit_or_transfer.purpose: Quick Steps for correcting a deposit or transfer by reversing it and entering the correct one.
scr_cash_reversing_a_deposit_or_transfer.rootCause: Cash transactions cannot be edited after saving; reversal is the standard correction.
scr_cash_reversing_a_deposit_or_transfer.ifSkipped: Errors remain or are fixed with untraceable JEs.

scr_cash_adding_a_manual_payment_2.purpose: Quick Steps for using a manual payment to quickly add a bill and record its payment in one step.
scr_cash_adding_a_manual_payment_2.rootCause: Urgent payments happen outside the check run; the quick path makes recording them easy so they are not skipped.
scr_cash_adding_a_manual_payment_2.ifSkipped: Urgent payments go unrecorded and are paid twice.

scr_cash_generating_a_payment_file_2.purpose: Quick Steps for generating the ACH or electronic payment file that contains approved vendor payments, ready for transmission to the bank before the cut-off.
scr_cash_generating_a_payment_file_2.outcome: Payment files created before bank cut-off.
scr_cash_generating_a_payment_file_2.rootCause: ACH files must reach the bank before its cut-off to settle on the intended date. A short, repeatable procedure reduces the delays that occur when file generation depends on someone looking up the steps each time.
scr_cash_generating_a_payment_file_2.ifSkipped: Late payment files mean vendors are paid a day or more late.

scr_cash_adding_a_receipt_2.purpose: Quick Steps for recording miscellaneous revenue that cannot be booked in Leasing & Rents — laundry, vending, insurance proceeds, vendor refunds.
scr_cash_adding_a_receipt_2.outcome: Non-resident receipts recorded promptly and correctly.
scr_cash_adding_a_receipt_2.rootCause: Non-resident receipts do not flow through Leasing & Rents; without a quick path they become unexplained bank deposits.
scr_cash_adding_a_receipt_2.ifSkipped: Unexplained deposits appear on bank recs and income is understated.

scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_transactio.purpose: Quick Steps for recording a charge against a company credit card — card, date, merchant, amount, property and GL coding — as soon as the purchase is made.
scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_transactio.outcome: Card charges recorded and coded to the right property in the month they occur.
scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_transactio.rootCause: Card statements arrive weeks after purchases. Recording charges as they happen puts the expense in the correct month and lets managers review spending before the statement is paid.
scr_cash_adding_a_credit_card_transactio.ifSkipped: Card expenses land a month late and unreviewed spending is paid with the statement.

scr_cash_adding_a_charge_payoff_2.purpose: Quick Steps for selecting the credit card charges to be paid and recording the payment to the card issuer against those specific charges.
scr_cash_adding_a_charge_payoff_2.outcome: Card balances paid against identified charges.
scr_cash_adding_a_charge_payoff_2.rootCause: Paying the issuer a lump sum without tying it to charges leaves the card liability impossible to reconcile to the statement; selecting charges keeps unpaid items visible before late fees accrue.
scr_cash_adding_a_charge_payoff_2.ifSkipped: Lump-sum payments cannot be reconciled to statements.

scr_cash_customizing_and_running_a_regis.purpose: Quick Steps for running bank, check, deposit, receipts or credit card registers with the right filters.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_a_regis.outcome: Register reports produced for reconciliation and review.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_a_regis.rootCause: Registers support reconciliations and audits; the quick path makes them easy to produce correctly.
scr_cash_customizing_and_running_a_regis.ifSkipped: Registers are run with wrong filters and do not support the reconciliation.
redFlags: Register periods not matching the reconciliation

scr_cash_adding_bank_interest_and_charge.purpose: Quick Steps for entering bank service charges, wire fees, analysis fees and interest earned from the monthly bank statement, so they are recorded before the reconciliation.
scr_cash_adding_bank_interest_and_charge.outcome: Bank-originated items recorded monthly so the reconciliation can clear.
scr_cash_adding_bank_interest_and_charge.rootCause: Bank fees and interest never pass through A/P or A/R; they become recurring reconciling items unless someone records them from the statement every month.
scr_cash_adding_bank_interest_and_charge.ifSkipped: The same fee items reappear as reconciling items every month and bank charges are missing from the P&L.

scr_cash_adding_credit_card_charges_and_.purpose: Quick Steps for entering the monthly interest and fees shown on company credit card statements — late fees, annual fees, finance charges — before reconciling the card.
scr_cash_adding_credit_card_charges_and_.outcome: Card fees and interest recorded so the card reconciliation balances.
scr_cash_adding_credit_card_charges_and_.rootCause: Card fees appear only on issuer statements and must be entered before the reconciliation; recurring late fees also signal that card payments are being made late.
scr_cash_adding_credit_card_charges_and_.ifSkipped: Card reconciliations do not balance and late-payment patterns go unnoticed.
reports: Credit card charges and fees list

scr_cash_reconciling_a_bank_account.purpose: Quick Steps for making sure the monthly bank statement matches the books — select the account, load statement data, match, resolve differences and finalize.
scr_cash_reconciling_a_bank_account.rootCause: Bank recs are the most important monthly cash control; a quick guide keeps the process consistent across preparers.
scr_cash_reconciling_a_bank_account.ifSkipped: Recs performed inconsistently and errors missed.

scr_cash_reconciling_a_credit_card.purpose: Quick Steps for reconciling a company credit card: enter miscellaneous statement charges and fees, then match recorded transactions to the issuer statement until the balance agrees.
scr_cash_reconciling_a_credit_card.outcome: Card liability agrees with the issuer statement.
scr_cash_reconciling_a_credit_card.rootCause: Company cards bypass purchase orders and invoice approval. Monthly reconciliation to the issuer statement is where unrecorded, duplicated or unauthorized charges are caught before they become a pattern.
scr_cash_reconciling_a_credit_card.ifSkipped: Card liabilities misstated and misuse undetected.

scr_cash_creating_reconciliation_rules.purpose: Quick Steps for setting up reconciliation rules and pairing them into rule sets for bank accounts.
scr_cash_creating_reconciliation_rules.rootCause: Rules are the key to reconciling at scale; a quick guide encourages consistent setup.
scr_cash_creating_reconciliation_rules.ifSkipped: Accounts remain on manual matching and recs miss the close deadline.
redFlags: Rules created without testing on a prior month

scr_cash_escheating_invoices.purpose: Quick Steps for escheating aged, unclaimed payments — moving them to aged payables, performing due diligence, remitting to the state and marking them escheated.
scr_cash_escheating_invoices.outcome: Unclaimed property handled in line with state law.
scr_cash_escheating_invoices.rootCause: Unclaimed property compliance is legally required and audited by states; a quick guide keeps the multi-step process consistent.
scr_cash_escheating_invoices.ifSkipped: Stale items remain or are voided to income, creating state audit exposure.

scr_cash_scheduling_positive_pay_files.purpose: Quick Steps for setting up positive pay to generate or schedule issued-check files to the bank.
scr_cash_scheduling_positive_pay_files.outcome: Positive pay files sent automatically after check runs.
scr_cash_scheduling_positive_pay_files.rootCause: Scheduled positive pay removes reliance on manual generation after every check run.
scr_cash_scheduling_positive_pay_files.ifSkipped: Some check runs are not reported and checks are unprotected.

scr_cash_calculating_a_locations_availab.purpose: Quick Steps for calculating a property's available cash — cash less holdbacks plus external balances — for distributions or funding.
scr_cash_calculating_a_locations_availab.outcome: A quick available cash figure for a decision.
scr_cash_calculating_a_locations_availab.rootCause: Asset managers request available cash frequently; the quick path gives a consistent calculation.
scr_cash_calculating_a_locations_availab.ifSkipped: Available cash calculated inconsistently in spreadsheets.

scr_cash_bank_reconciliations.purpose: Bank reconciliation quick help: what to do when the Amount to Reconcile is not zero — confirm the beginning balance, statement date and ending balance, compare book to G/L, and find missing transactions.
scr_cash_bank_reconciliations.outcome: A structured path to find why a rec does not balance.
scr_cash_bank_reconciliations.rootCause: Unbalanced recs are the most common cash problem; a fixed diagnostic sequence gets preparers to the cause without guessing.
scr_cash_bank_reconciliations.ifSkipped: Preparers guess at the cause or plug the difference to a suspense account.

scr_cash_step_1_confirm_the_beginning_ba.purpose: Diagnostic step 1: confirm the rec's beginning balance equals the prior reconciliation's ending balance and the bank's prior statement ending balance.
scr_cash_step_1_confirm_the_beginning_ba.outcome: Breaks caused by changes to prior periods are identified immediately.
scr_cash_step_1_confirm_the_beginning_ba.rootCause: Beginning balance mismatches mean a prior rec was changed or a transaction was posted into a reconciled period — a different problem from current-month errors.
scr_cash_step_1_confirm_the_beginning_ba.ifSkipped: Preparers search the current month for an error that actually sits in a prior period.
redFlags: Beginning balance different from prior ending balance

scr_cash_step_2_confirm_the_statement_en.purpose: Diagnostic step 2: confirm the statement ending date and ending balance keyed into the rec match the bank statement exactly.
scr_cash_step_2_confirm_the_statement_en.outcome: Keying errors in statement data are eliminated as a cause.
scr_cash_step_2_confirm_the_statement_en.rootCause: Keying the wrong ending balance (e.g., the available balance instead of the ledger balance) is a frequent cause of unbalanced recs.
scr_cash_step_2_confirm_the_statement_en.ifSkipped: Preparers chase transaction differences caused by a typo.
redFlags: Available balance used instead of ledger balance

scr_cash_step_3_compare_the_book_balance.purpose: Diagnostic step 3: compare the reconciliation's book balance to the G/L cash account balance for the same date.
scr_cash_step_3_compare_the_book_balance.outcome: Differences caused by entries dated outside the period or posted to cash outside Cash Management are identified.
scr_cash_step_3_compare_the_book_balance.rootCause: JEs posted directly to cash, or transactions dated after the statement date, make the book balance differ from the G/L.
scr_cash_step_3_compare_the_book_balance.ifSkipped: Book-to-G/L differences remain hidden and the rec does not tie to the balance sheet.

scr_cash_step_4_identify_missing_transac.purpose: Diagnostic step 4: find transactions on the bank statement not in the books (fees, NSF returns, auto-debits) or in the books but not at the bank.
scr_cash_step_4_identify_missing_transac.outcome: Missing transactions are recorded or explained.
scr_cash_step_4_identify_missing_transac.rootCause: After data-entry causes are ruled out, remaining differences are almost always missing transactions on one side.
scr_cash_step_4_identify_missing_transac.ifSkipped: Missing transactions stay unrecorded and the rec remains out of balance.

scr_cash_faqs.purpose: Bank reconciliation FAQs, including the AUTO CONTRA entry that appears on the first reconciliation representing the net of prior activity.
scr_cash_faqs.outcome: Users understand system-generated entries on first reconciliations.
scr_cash_faqs.rootCause: The AUTO CONTRA entry confuses new users; understanding it prevents incorrect adjustments on first recs.
scr_cash_faqs.ifSkipped: Users reverse or adjust AUTO CONTRA entries incorrectly.

scr_cash_summary.purpose: One-page summary of what to check when a bank reconciliation's Amount to Reconcile is not zero: beginning balance, statement ending date and balance, book versus G/L, and missing transactions — in that order.
scr_cash_summary.outcome: Preparers have a short, memorable checklist to follow before escalating an unbalanced rec.
scr_cash_summary.rootCause: Under close pressure, preparers skip straight to searching transactions. A short checklist enforces the order that finds the cause fastest — most differences are in the first two checks.
scr_cash_summary.ifSkipped: Diagnosis is haphazard, recs are escalated prematurely, and some are plugged instead of fixed.
redFlags: Recs escalated without completing the checklist
